# Hydrogen — calculated thermodynamic functions

<!-- generated-by: sync-thermochemistry.mjs -->

Source: SRC-000508, NIST Chemistry WebBook / Chase (1998), retrieved 2026-10-05. These are calculations from dated fits, not new measurements. Values below are rounded to four decimal places for computational comparison; this is not a statement of physical precision. Uncertainty: UNKNOWN. Basis: **mol H2**.

[Full calculation and limits](../0001-Hydrogen-H-Thermochemistry.md) · [Complete 101-point-per-fit CSV](0001-Hydrogen-H-TABLE-010-Thermodynamic-Functions.csv) · [Exact coefficients](../data/structured/0001-Hydrogen-H-NIST-Thermochemistry.yaml)

sources.scope_note: A dated 5 October 2026 thermochemistry retrieval of the existing NIST molecular-Hydrogen work. Its thermal mask and retained comparison table are separate from the unchanged 16 September spectroscopy retrieval. This is a source revision/scope link, not independent corroborating evidence.
sources.title: NIST Chemistry WebBook — molecular Hydrogen H2 gas thermochemistry (5 October 2026 retrieval)
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.scope: Neutral molecular H2 only; not atomic H, an ion or elemental composition averaged over species. One mole of H2 contains two moles of H atoms. UNSPECIFIED-IN-RETAINED-SHOMATE-TABLE. Other-name aliases o-Hydrogen and p-Hydrogen do not assign the three fits to normal, para, ortho or equilibrium H2 and do not establish any numeric spin fraction. The page labels separate gas entropy reference data at 1 bar. The Shomate equations carry standard-state superscripts and no pressure input; an applied sample pressure or arbitrary-pressure EOS is not supplied. Only GAS Shomate fits are supplied, 298–6000 K. Do not extrapolate to the 20.271 K equilibrium-H2 boiling point, cryogenic liquid/solid, phase changes or spin conversion. The coefficients provide no coefficient uncertainties or covariance; quantity uncertainty remains UNKNOWN. Publisher rounding and numerical derivative residuals are software/source-format checks, not physical uncertainty.
sources.reference: Chase, M.W., Jr. (1998), NIST-JANAF Thermochemical Tables, Fourth Edition. Fit comment: Data last reviewed in March, 1977; New parameter fit October 2001.
